classification_basis: Implemented entries were reviewed against the official page, fixtures, and both engines. Summaries, analysis classes, and delegation recommendations for unimplemented entries were drafted from the official page and assigned a status by the documented rules in docs/architecture/sei-cert-rule-pack.md; review them against the official page before promoting an entry.

rules.title: Do not destroy a mutex while it is locked
rules.summary: A mutex must not be destroyed while any thread owns it or waits on it; its lifetime must exceed every thread that may lock it.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Local or member mutex goes out of scope or is deleted while detached threads may still hold or acquire it.
rules.compliant_concept: Mutex has static or otherwise longer lifetime, or all using threads are joined before destruction.
false_positive_risks: Paths on which the lock call failed but the code continues to destroy are reported.
false_negative_risks: std::mutex objects whose lifetime ends while locked require lifetime analysis.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Same-function POSIX lock followed by destroy without an intervening unlock in C++ code.

rules.title: Ensure actively held locks are released on exceptional conditions
rules.summary: A held mutex must be released on every exit path, including when an exception propagates out of the critical section.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Manual lock() followed by code that may throw before the matching unlock() call.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses RAII guards such as lock_guard or unique_lock, or catches, unlocks, and rethrows.
false_positive_risks: A throw that is caught inside the same scope before the lock matters may be reported.
false_negative_risks: Exceptions raised by functions called while the lock is held are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Manual lock() followed by a throw without an intervening unlock().

rules.title: Prevent data races when accessing bit-fields from multiple threads
rules.summary: Adjacent bit-fields sharing a memory location must not be accessed concurrently by different threads without common synchronization.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Two threads write different bit-fields of the same struct unprotected, or under different mutexes.
rules.compliant_concept: Protects all bit-fields sharing storage with one mutex, or uses separate non-bit-field members.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Bit-field writes in single-threaded code or already serialized by a shared lock would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Determining which threads touch which bit-fields and storage-unit sharing requires layout and thread reasoning.

rules.title: Avoid deadlock by locking in a predefined order
rules.summary: When several mutexes are acquired together, every thread must acquire them in one consistent global order, or use a deadlock-avoiding multi-lock.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Different code paths lock the same pair of mutexes in opposite orders, enabling circular wait.
rules.compliant_concept: Locks in a fixed ordering (e.g., by address or rank) or uses std::lock / scoped_lock.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Nested lock acquisitions that are always ordered consistently would be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Lock order inversions across functions, objects aliased at runtime, or argument-dependent order are missed.

rules.title: Wrap functions that can spuriously wake up in a loop
rules.summary: Condition-variable waits that can wake spuriously must be guarded by re-checking the condition predicate, via a loop or the predicate overload.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calls wait/wait_for/wait_until once inside an if or unguarded, without re-testing the predicate.
rules.compliant_concept: Waits inside a while loop testing the predicate, or passes a predicate to wait.
false_positive_risks: A wait guarded by a loop in a caller is reported.
false_negative_risks: A loop that does not re-test the predicate is accepted as compliant.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Predicate-free condition-variable waits not lexically inside a loop.

rules.title: Preserve thread safety and liveness when using condition variables
rules.summary: Notification of condition variables must wake the thread(s) whose predicate became true; notify_one is safe only when any waiter can proceed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses notify_one when waiters have different predicates, so the wrong thread may wake and others starve.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses notify_all, or separate condition variables per distinct predicate.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Every notify_one call would look suspicious even when all waiters share one predicate.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Whether waiters share the same predicate depends on cross-function, cross-thread design not visible syntactically.

rules.title: Do not speculatively lock a non-recursive mutex that is already owned by the calling thread
rules.summary: A thread must not call a try_lock-family function on a non-recursive mutex it already owns.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calls try_lock on a std::mutex or timed_mutex while the same thread holds that mutex.
rules.compliant_concept: Restructures so try_lock occurs only when unowned, or uses a recursive mutex.
false_positive_risks: None expected for the declared non-recursive mutex types.
false_negative_risks: Re-locking through called functions or aliases, and std::unique_lock ownership, is not tracked.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Same-function lock() followed by another lock or try_lock on the same non-recursive mutex.

rules.title: Guarantee that container indices and iterators are within the valid range
rules.summary: Container subscripts and iterator positions must be validated to lie within the container's valid range before access.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Indexes a vector or array with an unchecked or possibly negative value, or advances past end.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks the index against size() with an unsigned type, or uses at() with exception handling.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Every operator[] use would be flagged even when bounds are established by loop structure or prior checks.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Index values flowing from callers or arithmetic need range analysis that syntax cannot provide.

rules.title: Use valid references, pointers, and iterators to reference elements of a container
rules.summary: References, pointers, and iterators into a container must not be used after an operation that may invalidate them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Keeps an iterator across insert/push_back/erase on the same container and then dereferences or increments it.
rules.compliant_concept: Refreshes iterators from the invalidating call's return value or re-obtains them after modification.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Modifications of containers whose invalidation rules spare the held iterator (e.g., list insert) look identical.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Aliased containers, modifications in callees, or reallocation-dependent invalidation are missed.

rules.title: Guarantee that library functions do not overflow
rules.summary: Library algorithms that write into a destination must have a destination guaranteed large enough, or use an inserting iterator.
rules.noncompliant_concept: std::copy or fill_n into an empty or undersized container via begin() with an unchecked count.
rules.compliant_concept: Sizes the destination first or uses back_inserter/insert so the container grows.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Algorithm calls writing via begin() into containers already resized elsewhere would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Destination size depends on runtime values and prior resize/reserve calls that syntax cannot relate.

rules.title: Use valid iterator ranges
rules.summary: Iterator ranges passed to algorithms or container operations must come from the same container, with begin not after end, and be valid.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passes (a.begin(), b.end()) or a reversed/invalidated pair as a range.
rules.compliant_concept: Derives both range endpoints from the same live container in proper order.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Different-looking expressions that alias the same container (references, getters) may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Iterators stored in variables or passed from callers lose provenance; ordering needs value reasoning.

rules.title: Do not subtract iterators that do not refer to the same container
rules.summary: Iterators or pointers may only be subtracted or relationally compared when both refer into the same container or array object.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Subtracts or compares pointers/iterators from distinct objects, e.g., to test whether one lies within a range.
rules.compliant_concept: Restricts arithmetic to same-object iterators, or tests membership via equality loops or std::less.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pointer subtractions within one buffer are syntactically identical to cross-object ones.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Provenance of pointers passed through parameters or containers cannot be established without dataflow.

rules.title: Do not use an additive operator on an iterator if the result would overflow
rules.summary: Adding to or subtracting from an iterator must not move it beyond the container's valid range, including past end.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Advances an iterator by an unchecked offset, e.g., begin() + n where n may exceed size().
rules.compliant_concept: Checks the offset against distance to end before arithmetic, or clamps with std::min.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Iterator arithmetic preceded by size checks in other statements may still be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Offsets originating from callers or computations need range analysis unavailable to syntax.

rules.title: Do not use pointer arithmetic on polymorphic objects
rules.summary: Pointer arithmetic and array subscripting must not be performed through a pointer to a polymorphic base when elements are of derived type.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Iterates an array of derived objects using a base-class pointer with ++ or [i].
rules.compliant_concept: Stores derived-typed arrays and uses derived pointers, or uses containers of (smart) pointers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Without type info, any pointer arithmetic on class pointers would match, including non-polymorphic or final types.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Base pointer origin and whether the class is polymorphic require resolved types.

rules.title: Provide a valid ordering predicate
rules.summary: Comparison predicates given to ordered containers or sorting algorithms must implement a strict weak ordering.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses <= or >= in a comparator, or a comparator lacking transitivity or irreflexivity.
rules.compliant_concept: Comparator uses strict < semantics consistently, e.g., via std::tie lexicographic comparison.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Comparators using <= for non-ordering purposes or in helper code may be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Non-transitive logic spread across several comparisons or functions is undetectable syntactically.

rules.title: Predicate function objects should not be mutable
rules.summary: Predicate function objects passed to algorithms must not depend on mutable internal state, since algorithms may copy them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passes a stateful functor or mutable lambda whose result depends on how many times it was invoked.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses stateless predicates, or holds shared state externally via references or reference_wrapper.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Mutable lambdas whose state does not affect the predicate result would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Stateful functor classes defined elsewhere and passed by name are not recognizable without types.

rules.title: Do not define a C-style variadic function
rules.summary: Do not define functions with a C-style ellipsis parameter; use variadic templates or other type-safe alternatives.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Defines a function whose parameter list ends in ... and uses va_list.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses a function parameter pack or fixed overloads instead of an ellipsis.

exceptions.summary: C-style variadic functions are allowed when they have extern "C" linkage, e.g. C APIs in C++.
Variadic functions declared but never defined, used in unevaluated contexts like SFINAE, are allowed.

false_positive_risks: A definition whose parameter list is spelled through macros may be misread.
false_negative_risks: Definitions whose braces nest the extern "C" block in macros, or whose parameter list is produced by macros, are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Every C-style variadic function definition, including members and trailing-return forms; declarations and extern "C" definitions are excluded per the rule's exceptions.

rules.title: Do not declare or define a reserved identifier
rules.summary: Do not declare, define, #define, or #undef identifiers reserved to the implementation or names from standard headers and keywords.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses names with double underscores, leading underscore plus capital, or redefines standard names/keywords via macros.
rules.compliant_concept: Chooses identifiers outside reserved patterns and leaves standard names untouched.

exceptions.summary: Macros named like reserved identifiers are fine for compatibility when semantics are unchanged.
Compiler vendors and standard-library authors may use implementation-reserved identifiers.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Header guards and compatibility macros with leading underscores, or code inside implementation headers, may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Global-namespace names beginning with a single underscore need scope awareness; macro-generated names are missed.

rules.title: Never qualify a reference type with const or volatile
rules.summary: Reference types must not be given const or volatile qualifiers directly; cv-qualify the referenced type instead.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writes a declaration like 'char &const p', applying const to the reference itself.
rules.compliant_concept: Qualifies the referred-to type, e.g. 'const char &p'.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Few; typedef or decltype-introduced qualifiers are syntactically different and legitimately ignored.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: cv-qualification applied through typedef or template parameters escapes syntactic matching.

rules.title: Do not write syntactically ambiguous declarations
rules.summary: Avoid declarations that parse ambiguously as function declarations or as unnamed temporaries (vexing parses).
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writes 'T obj();' or 'Lock(m);' intending an object, getting a function declaration or immediately-destroyed temporary.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses brace initialization or named variables so the declaration means what is intended.
false_positive_risks: None expected for the matched lock types.
false_negative_risks: The vexing parse T obj(); and other ambiguous declarations are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Parenthesized standard lock declarations that declare a variable named after the mutex.

rules.title: Overload allocation and deallocation functions as a pair in the same scope
rules.summary: When an allocation function is overloaded in a scope, the matching deallocation function must be overloaded in the same scope, and vice versa.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Class defines operator new without a corresponding operator delete (or placement form without its pair).
rules.compliant_concept: Declares allocation and deallocation overloads together in the same class or namespace scope.

exceptions.summary: A placement deallocation function may be omitted when allocation and construction cannot throw.
An allocation/deallocation counterpart identical to the default may be omitted, with an explanatory comment.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pairs split across a class and its base, or intentionally default-equivalent overloads, may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Overloads introduced via macros or inherited scopes may be missed without semantic lookup.

rules.title: Avoid information leakage when passing a class object across a trust boundary
rules.summary: Objects copied across a trust boundary must not expose uninitialized padding bytes or other unintended bytes of their representation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Copies a struct with padding to user space or the network after member-wise initialization only.
rules.compliant_concept: Zero-fills the whole object first, serializes members individually, or uses packed layouts deliberately.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Raw copies of structs without padding, or whose bytes are fully initialized, would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Padding depends on layout and alignment; identifying trust boundaries requires domain knowledge.

rules.title: Avoid cycles during initialization of static objects
rules.summary: Initialization of static or thread-storage objects must not recursively re-enter its own initialization or depend cyclically on other statics.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A function-local static's initializer calls back into the same function, or globals initialize from each other across TUs.
rules.compliant_concept: Removes initialization cycles, uses constant initialization, or lazily computes values without re-entry.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Static initializers calling functions that do not actually re-enter would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Cycles through call chains and across translation units require whole-program call graphs.

rules.title: Do not let exceptions escape from destructors or deallocation functions
rules.summary: Destructors and deallocation functions must not allow exceptions to escape them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A destructor or operator delete throws, or calls a throwing function without catching, or is noexcept(false).
rules.compliant_concept: Catches and handles all exceptions inside destructors and deallocators, keeping them noexcept.
false_positive_risks: Destructors explicitly declared noexcept(false) whose callers handle the exception are reported.
false_negative_risks: Exceptions propagated from called functions and from deallocation functions are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: throw expressions directly inside a destructor body and not inside a try block.

rules.title: Do not modify the standard namespaces
rules.summary: Do not add declarations or definitions to namespace std or posix except permitted template specializations for user-defined types.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Declares new functions, types, or specializations involving only standard types inside namespace std.
rules.compliant_concept: Places code in own namespaces; only specializes std templates on program-defined types where allowed.
false_positive_risks: Declarations inside std blocks nested more than four brace levels deep, or specializations with unusual spellings, may be misclassified.
false_negative_risks: New class definitions and specializations involving only standard types in namespace std are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Variable and function declarations or definitions added to namespace std or posix.

rules.title: Do not define an unnamed namespace in a header file
rules.summary: Header files must not contain unnamed namespaces, since each including translation unit gets its own distinct copy.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A .h/.hpp file declares 'namespace { ... }'.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses named namespaces with inline or extern declarations in headers, keeping unnamed namespaces in source files.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Headers included only once, or non-header files with header extensions, may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Header-ness is decided by file extension; included .inc/.cpp files or nonstandard extensions are missed.

rules.title: Obey the one-definition rule
rules.summary: Each entity must have exactly one definition program-wide, and inline or class definitions repeated across translation units must be token- and meaning-identical.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Different translation units define the same class, inline function, or template differently.
rules.compliant_concept: Defines shared entities once in headers with identical content, keeping TU-local items internal.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Same-named entities in distinct namespaces or with internal linkage could be mistaken for duplicates.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: ODR violations emerge only across translation units, macros, and build configurations.

rules.title: Do not abruptly terminate the program
rules.summary: Programs must not terminate abruptly via abort, quick_exit, _Exit, or implicit std::terminate, bypassing cleanup.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calls std::abort or quick_exit, or lets exceptions reach terminate via noexcept violations or uncaught throws.
rules.compliant_concept: Propagates errors to main and returns, or throws exceptions that are caught and handled.

exceptions.summary: After reporting the problem, abort, _Exit, or terminate may be called for unrecoverable critical errors.

false_positive_risks: Calls permitted by ERR50-CPP-EX1 (after reporting an unrecoverable error) are reported for review.
false_negative_risks: Implicit std::terminate paths (uncaught exceptions, noexcept violations, exceptions from exit handlers) need exception-flow analysis.
std::exit after automatic objects are initialized is not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

rules.title: Handle all exceptions
rules.summary: Every thrown exception must be caught by some handler; none may propagate out of main or a thread entry function.
rules.noncompliant_concept: main or a thread function lets exceptions escape without a catch-all handler.
rules.compliant_concept: Wraps main and thread bodies in try blocks catching all exceptions and terminating cleanly.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Entry points that call only noexcept code would be flagged for missing catch-all.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Determining which exceptions callees throw requires interprocedural analysis.

rules.title: Do not use setjmp() or longjmp()
rules.summary: Do not use setjmp or longjmp in C++ code.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calls setjmp/longjmp to implement nonlocal control transfer.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses C++ exceptions or structured returns for nonlocal error handling.
false_positive_risks: None expected; the rule forbids the facility outright.
false_negative_risks: Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.
Calls through function pointers are not detected.

implementation.coverage_note: Every setjmp/longjmp-family use in C++ is reported.

rules.title: Do not reference base classes or class data members in a constructor or destructor function-try-block handler
rules.summary: Handlers of constructor or destructor function-try-blocks must not reference non-static members or base classes of the object.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A constructor's function-try-block catch handler reads or writes a data member.
rules.compliant_concept: Handles cleanup in member destructors or uses only parameters and statics in the handler.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: References to static members or same-named locals/parameters could be mistaken for member access.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Implicit this-> member accesses need name lookup to distinguish from locals.

rules.title: Catch handlers should order their parameter types from most derived to least derived
rules.summary: Catch clauses in one try block must list more-derived exception types before their base classes.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A catch for a base class precedes a catch for a class derived from it, making it unreachable.
rules.compliant_concept: Orders handlers from most derived to least derived.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Unrelated types with similar names could be flagged by name-based heuristics.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Inheritance relationships require class hierarchy resolution.

rules.title: Honor exception specifications
rules.summary: Functions must not throw exceptions their exception specification disallows, including from noexcept functions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A noexcept function calls something that can throw without catching it.
rules.compliant_concept: Catches all exceptions within noexcept functions, or relaxes the specification accurately.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Calls in noexcept functions to functions that never actually throw would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Exception sets of callees are unknown without interprocedural analysis.

rules.title: Guarantee exception safety
rules.summary: Code must provide at least the basic exception guarantee: if an exception is thrown, objects remain valid and no resources or invariants are broken.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Mutates object state, then calls a throwing operation, leaving invariants broken or memory dangling on throw.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses copy-and-swap, RAII, and ordering so state changes commit only after throwing work succeeds.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pattern matches on delete-before-new sequences flag code where the throwing call cannot fail.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Invariant breakage depends on class semantics and throw points across functions.

rules.title: Do not leak resources when handling exceptions
rules.summary: Resources acquired must be released if an exception is thrown, including when constructors fail partway through.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Raw new or resource acquisition followed by code that can throw before the matching release.
rules.compliant_concept: Manages resources with RAII objects or smart pointers so unwinding releases them.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Raw allocations followed by non-throwing code are flagged even though no leak path exists.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Which calls can throw, and resources acquired in callees, require interprocedural knowledge.

rules.title: Handle all exceptions thrown before main() begins executing
rules.summary: Exceptions thrown while constructing or destroying static- or thread-storage objects cannot be caught by main; such initializers must not throw.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A global or namespace-scope object's constructor can throw, e.g., a std::string initialized from input.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses constexpr/noexcept constructors for statics, or defers initialization into functions with handlers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Static objects whose constructors cannot throw in practice but lack noexcept may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Whether a constructor may throw depends on resolved overloads and callee behavior.

rules.title: Do not throw an exception across execution boundaries
rules.summary: Exceptions must not propagate across execution boundaries such as C APIs, shared libraries built with different toolchains, or callbacks.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Lets an exception escape an extern "C" function or callback invoked by foreign code.
rules.compliant_concept: Catches all exceptions at the boundary and converts them to error codes.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: extern "C" functions that call only non-throwing code may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Boundaries like DLL exports or callback registration are not identifiable syntactically.

rules.title: Exception objects must be nothrow copy constructible
rules.summary: Types thrown as exceptions must have copy constructors that cannot throw.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Throws an object whose class has a member like std::string, making copying potentially throwing.
rules.compliant_concept: Throws types with noexcept copy constructors, e.g., holding a shared_ptr or deriving from std::runtime_error.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Exception classes whose copies never throw in practice but lack noexcept may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Copy-constructor noexcept-ness depends on resolved member types and class definitions.

rules.title: Catch exceptions by lvalue reference
rules.summary: Exceptions should be caught by lvalue reference, not by value or pointer, to avoid slicing and extra copying.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A catch clause declares its parameter by value, e.g. catch (std::exception e).
rules.compliant_concept: Catches by (const) lvalue reference, e.g. catch (const std::exception &e).
false_positive_risks: Trivial class types and typedefs of scalar types, which may be caught by value, are reported because the type is not resolved.
false_negative_risks: Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Every by-value handler whose type is not a reference, pointer, or fundamental type.

rules.title: Detect errors when converting a string to a number
rules.summary: String-to-number conversions must check for failure, out-of-range values, and unconsumed trailing characters.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses atoi/atol or stream extraction without checking stream state or end position.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses strtol/stoi or stream extraction with error-state, range, and trailing-input checks.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Stream extraction whose state is checked later or by a caller may be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Detecting missing fail-state checks after extraction needs control-flow reasoning.

rules.title: Do not depend on the order of evaluation for side effects
rules.summary: Correctness must not depend on unspecified or unsequenced evaluation order of operands or function arguments with side effects.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Modifies a variable and also reads or modifies it elsewhere in the same unsequenced expression or argument list.
rules.compliant_concept: Splits side effects into separate statements so ordering is explicit.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: C++17 sequencing makes some patterns (e.g., assignment, shifts) well-defined though they look suspicious.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Side effects inside called functions or via aliases are invisible to syntactic matching.

rules.title: Do not delete an array through a pointer of the incorrect type
rules.summary: Arrays must be deleted through a pointer whose static type matches the allocated element type.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Allocates new Derived[n] and deletes via a Base* with delete[].
rules.compliant_concept: Deletes through the original element type, or uses containers of smart pointers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Any delete[] on a base-typed pointer looks suspect even if the array truly holds base objects.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: The dynamic element type comes from allocation sites possibly far away.

rules.title: Do not rely on side effects in unevaluated operands
rules.summary: Do not write expressions with intended side effects as operands of sizeof, typeid on non-polymorphic types, noexcept, decltype, or similar unevaluated contexts.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Places an increment, assignment, or call inside sizeof or decltype expecting it to execute.
rules.compliant_concept: Performs side effects in separate statements and passes side-effect-free expressions to unevaluated operators.

exceptions.summary: Side-effecting expressions may be unevaluated operands in macros or SFINAE contexts.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Function calls in decltype or SFINAE expressions used purely for type deduction would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: typeid evaluation depends on whether the operand type is polymorphic, requiring types.

rules.title: Do not read uninitialized memory
rules.summary: Objects with indeterminate value, such as uninitialized locals or default-initialized heap memory, must not be read before being given a value.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Reads a local or newly allocated variable on a path where it was never assigned.
rules.compliant_concept: Initializes variables at declaration or ensures assignment on all paths before use.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Uninitialized declarations later assigned on all paths, or initialized via out-parameters, are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Path-sensitive reads, heap memory, and partial struct initialization need dataflow analysis.

rules.title: Do not access an object outside of its lifetime
rules.summary: Objects must not be accessed before their lifetime begins or after it ends, including dangling references to temporaries and locals.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Returns a reference to a local, binds to a destroyed temporary, or uses an object after destruction.
rules.compliant_concept: Returns by value, extends lifetimes correctly, and keeps referents alive while references are used.
false_positive_risks: Callers that never use the returned view or iterator are still reported, because every use would be outside the object's lifetime.
false_negative_risks: Use after explicit destructor calls, after scope exit, through thread_local or member pointers, and in placement-new storage requires lifetime analysis.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Returning views, raw pointers, or iterators into non-static local strings and vectors.

rules.title: Do not access a cv-qualified object through a cv-unqualified type
rules.summary: Objects defined const or volatile must not be accessed through glvalues that drop those qualifiers, e.g., by const_cast and modification.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses const_cast or C-style casts to strip const/volatile and then modifies or reads through the result.
rules.compliant_concept: Keeps qualifiers, uses mutable for logically-const members, or fixes APIs to be const-correct.

exceptions.summary: Casting away const is allowed to call a non-const legacy API that does not modify the object.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: const_cast used where the original object is non-const, or for read-only legacy API calls, is benign.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Whether the underlying object is really const-defined requires tracing to its definition.

rules.title: Do not call a function with a mismatched language linkage
rules.summary: Functions must only be called through pointers or declarations whose language linkage matches the function's definition.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passes a C++-linkage function where an extern "C" function pointer is expected, e.g., to a C callback API.
rules.compliant_concept: Declares callbacks for C APIs with extern "C" linkage.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Most compilers treat linkage as not part of the type, so many matches are practically harmless.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Linkage of function pointer types in casts or templates needs semantic analysis.

rules.title: Do not cast or delete pointers to incomplete classes
rules.summary: Pointers to incomplete class types must not be deleted or cast in ways requiring the complete definition.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Deletes or static_casts a pointer whose class is only forward-declared at that point.
rules.compliant_concept: Ensures the class is complete where deleted or cast, e.g., defining pimpl destructors in the source file.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Deletes in files where the type is complete through an included header would be flagged by naive matching.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Type completeness at a given point depends on includes and declarations requiring a full parse.

rules.title: Pass an object of the correct type to va_start
rules.summary: The last named parameter given to va_start must not be a reference, a type changed by default promotions, or a non-trivial class.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calls va_start with a reference parameter or a float/char/short or class-type parameter.
rules.compliant_concept: Ensures the last named parameter is a trivially copyable, promotion-stable value type.
false_positive_risks: None expected.
false_negative_risks: Non-trivially copyable class parameters and typedefs of promoted types require type resolution.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: va_start on a reference parameter or a parameter whose type undergoes default promotion.

rules.title: Use offsetof() on valid types and members
rules.summary: offsetof must only be applied to standard-layout types and to non-static, non-bit-field data members.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses offsetof on a class with virtual functions or mixed access, or on a static member or bit-field.
rules.compliant_concept: Restricts offsetof to standard-layout structs and regular data members.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Without type layout knowledge, any offsetof on a class looks suspicious.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Standard-layout status depends on full class definitions and inheritance.

rules.title: Do not pass a nonstandard-layout type object across execution boundaries
rules.summary: Objects of non-standard-layout type must not be passed to code compiled by a different compiler or language across an execution boundary.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passes a class with virtual functions or mixed access to an extern "C" or separately compiled library function.
rules.compliant_concept: Passes only standard-layout structures, or opaque handles, across boundaries.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Calls to separately compiled code with standard-layout arguments would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Layout properties and which functions cross boundaries require type and build knowledge.

rules.title: A lambda object must not outlive any of its reference captured objects
rules.summary: Lambdas capturing by reference must not be used after any reference-captured object has gone out of scope.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Returns or stores a lambda capturing locals by reference that is invoked after the function returns.
rules.compliant_concept: Captures by value, or ensures captured objects outlive every invocation.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Reference-capturing lambdas passed to synchronous algorithms are safe but match syntactically.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Lambdas stored in containers, std::function, or threads need escape and lifetime analysis.

rules.title: Do not access the bits of an object representation that are not part of the object's value representation
rules.summary: Code must not rely on bytes of an object that are not part of its value representation, such as padding or vtable pointers.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Compares or hashes class objects with memcmp, or memset/memcpy over objects with vptrs.
rules.compliant_concept: Compares members via operator== and copies via special member functions.

exceptions.summary: Object-representation bits may be accessed when unobservable, e.g. reading or writing only padding bits.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: memcmp/memcpy on padding-free trivially copyable types would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Padding and vptr presence depend on resolved type layouts.

rules.title: Do not rely on the value of a moved-from object
rules.summary: After an object is moved from, its value must not be relied upon until it is reassigned, except for types documenting a specified moved-from state.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Reads or uses a variable after passing it to std::move or a moving function.
rules.compliant_concept: Reinitializes moved-from objects before use, or only uses types like unique_ptr with defined moved-from states.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Uses after std::move where the callee did not actually move, or of types with specified states, are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Moves via rvalue-reference parameters without explicit std::move, and loop paths, need dataflow.

rules.title: Do not alternately input and output from a file stream without an intervening positioning call
rules.summary: On an update-mode file stream, switching between reading and writing requires an intervening flush or positioning operation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writes to an fstream then immediately reads (or vice versa) without seekg/seekp or flush.
rules.compliant_concept: Calls a seek or flush operation between alternating input and output.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Sequences where a positioning call occurs in a helper function may be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Read/write alternation across functions or loops requires stream state tracking.

rules.title: Close files when they are no longer needed
rules.summary: File streams opened by the program must be closed (explicitly or by destruction) before the program terminates or the stream object leaks.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calls std::terminate/exit or leaks a heap-allocated fstream while the file remains open.
rules.compliant_concept: Closes streams explicitly before termination or relies on scoped RAII stream objects.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Streams closed in destructors or other helpers may be flagged as unclosed.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Leaked stream objects or termination paths across functions need lifetime reasoning.

rules.title: Do not cast to an out-of-range enumeration value
rules.summary: Integer values must not be converted to an enumeration type unless they fall within that enumeration's range of valid values.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casts an arbitrary integer to an unfixed-underlying-type enum without validating its range.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks the value against the enumeration's valid range before casting, or uses fixed underlying types.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Casts to enums with fixed underlying types or with prior range checks would be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Enum range depends on enumerator values; integer values need range analysis.

rules.title: Do not access freed memory
rules.summary: Memory or objects must not be accessed through pointers or references after being deallocated or destroyed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Dereferences a pointer after delete/free, or uses c_str()/data() after the owning string changes.
rules.compliant_concept: Nulls or discards pointers after deallocation and uses ownership types with clear lifetimes.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Use after delete where the pointer was reassigned in between, or in other branches, would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Deallocation in callees, aliasing, and containers require interprocedural pointer analysis.

rules.title: Properly deallocate dynamically allocated resources
rules.summary: Dynamic resources must be released exactly once, using the deallocation function matching their allocation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Frees new memory with free, deletes new[] with delete, double-deletes, or deletes non-heap memory.
rules.compliant_concept: Pairs new/delete, new[]/delete[], malloc/free, or uses smart pointers with matching deleters.
false_positive_risks: None expected for same-variable pairings.
false_negative_risks: Double free, placement-new release, class-specific allocation functions, and pairings across functions require ownership analysis.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Same-function array new/scalar delete, malloc/delete, new/free, and unique_ptr<T> adopting new T[].

rules.title: Detect and handle memory allocation errors
rules.summary: Failure of memory allocation must be detected and handled, whether reported by null returns or by bad_alloc exceptions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses result of new(std::nothrow) or malloc without a null check, or lets bad_alloc escape unhandled.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks nothrow allocation results for null and catches bad_alloc where allocations may fail.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Allocations checked in a later statement or by a caller may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Null checks after aliasing, and exception handling in callers, require dataflow.

rules.title: Explicitly construct and destruct objects when manually managing object lifetime
rules.summary: When storage is managed manually, objects must be explicitly constructed before use and explicitly destroyed before their storage is released or reused.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casts malloc'd memory to a class pointer and uses it without placement new, or frees without calling the destructor.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses placement new to begin lifetime and explicitly invokes destructors before deallocation.

exceptions.summary: Explicit constructor or destructor calls are unnecessary for trivially constructible or destructible types.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags malloc/cast use on trivially constructible types, which is permitted.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Tracking whether constructor/destructor calls occur on each path requires dataflow and type triviality.

rules.title: Provide placement new with properly aligned pointers to sufficient storage capacity
rules.summary: Placement new must be given storage that is suitably aligned and large enough for the object or array being constructed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Constructs an object via placement new into a char buffer that is too small or misaligned.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses alignas-qualified storage of adequate size, or std::aligned_storage-like buffers with size checks.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Placement new into properly aligned storage declared elsewhere may still be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Size and alignment depend on types, array cookies, and buffer origins needing semantic analysis.

rules.title: Honor replacement dynamic storage management requirements
rules.summary: Replacement global allocation and deallocation functions must meet the standard's required behavior, e.g., throwing bad_alloc rather than returning null.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A replacement operator new returns nullptr on failure instead of throwing.
rules.compliant_concept: Replacement functions throw std::bad_alloc on failure and otherwise honor library contracts.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Nothrow-variant replacements, which may legitimately return null, may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Failure paths through helper allocators require dataflow to determine what is returned.

rules.title: Do not store an already-owned pointer value in an unrelated smart pointer
rules.summary: A pointer already owned by a smart pointer must not be handed to another unrelated smart pointer that would also manage it.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Constructs two shared_ptr or unique_ptr objects from the same raw pointer, or from get().
rules.compliant_concept: Copies the existing smart pointer, or uses enable_shared_from_this to share ownership.
false_positive_risks: A get() result passed to a smart pointer with a no-op deleter is reported.
false_negative_risks: Raw pointers obtained earlier and stored in variables are not tracked.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Smart pointers constructed, declared, or reset from another owner's get().

rules.title: Avoid using default operator new for over-aligned types
rules.summary: Over-aligned types must not be allocated with default operator new unless the implementation supports alignment-aware allocation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses new on an alignas(64)-style type in pre-C++17 code without class-specific operator new.
rules.compliant_concept: Provides aligned allocation operators or uses C++17 aligned new.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags C++17 or later code where aligned new is automatic.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Alignment of types via typedefs or templates requires resolved types.

rules.title: Do not use std::rand() for generating pseudorandom numbers
rules.summary: Do not use std::rand for pseudorandom numbers with quality or security requirements; use a proper generator.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calls rand()/std::rand() to produce random values.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses <random> engines such as std::mt19937 seeded properly, or a CSPRNG for security uses.
false_positive_risks: Uses of std::rand() for non-security purposes are reported; the rule makes no such distinction.
false_negative_risks: Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.
Calls through function pointers are not detected.

implementation.coverage_note: Every std::rand()/rand() call in C++ is reported.

rules.title: Ensure your random number generator is properly seeded
rules.summary: Pseudorandom generators must be seeded from an unpredictable source, not left default-seeded or seeded with constants.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Default-constructs a random engine or seeds it with a literal or time value.
rules.compliant_concept: Seeds engines from std::random_device or another high-entropy source.
false_positive_risks: Engines used only for reproducible simulations or tests are reported.
false_negative_risks: Direct initialization written as engine(std::time(nullptr)) is not parsed as a declaration by either engine.
Constant seeds supplied through variables and engines declared as class members are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

rules.title: Value-returning functions must return a value from all exit paths
rules.summary: Every control path in a non-void function must return a value; flowing off the end is undefined behavior.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A non-void function, or function-try-block handler, can reach the closing brace without returning.
rules.compliant_concept: Adds return statements on all paths, or ends paths with throw or noreturn calls.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Paths ending in non-annotated never-returning calls or exhaustive switches may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Reachability through complex control flow needs CFG analysis beyond syntax.

rules.title: Do not return from a function declared \[\[noreturn\]\]
rules.summary: Functions declared [[noreturn]] must never return to their caller.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A [[noreturn]] function has a path that falls off its end or executes return.
rules.compliant_concept: Ensures every path in such functions throws, loops forever, or calls another noreturn function.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Paths ending in calls to unannotated but non-returning functions may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Return paths depending on conditions or callee behavior need control-flow analysis.

rules.title: A signal handler must be a plain old function
rules.summary: Signal handlers must be plain old functions using only the C/C++ common subset with C linkage, avoiding C++-only features.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Registers a handler that uses exceptions, std::string, new, or has C++ linkage.
rules.compliant_concept: Registers extern "C" handlers that only set volatile sig_atomic_t or lock-free atomics.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Handlers calling safe helper functions may be flagged if helpers cannot be inspected.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: C++ features reached through called functions require interprocedural analysis.

rules.title: Do not invoke virtual functions from constructors or destructors
rules.summary: Constructors and destructors must not make unqualified virtual calls on the object under construction or destruction.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A constructor or destructor calls a virtual member function, directly or through helpers.
rules.compliant_concept: Calls non-virtual helpers, or qualifies the call explicitly when the current class's version is intended.

exceptions.summary: Virtual calls in constructors or destructors are allowed using an explicitly qualified name.
Virtual functions marked final, or in final classes, may be called during construction or destruction.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Calls to qualified, final, or non-virtual members look identical without type info.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Virtual calls made indirectly from helper functions require interprocedural analysis.

rules.title: Do not slice derived objects
rules.summary: Derived-class objects must not be copied into base-class objects by value, losing derived state.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passes, assigns, or catches a derived object by value as the base type.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses references, pointers, or smart pointers to the base, or clone patterns.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: By-value base parameters that never receive derived objects may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Derived-to-base relationships require class hierarchy and overload resolution.

rules.title: Do not delete a polymorphic object without a virtual destructor
rules.summary: Objects of derived type must not be deleted through a base-class pointer unless the base destructor is virtual.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Deletes via Base* where Base has a non-virtual destructor and the object is Derived.
rules.compliant_concept: Declares the base destructor virtual, or protected and non-virtual to forbid base deletion.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Deletes through base pointers that never point at derived objects would be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Virtual-ness of destructors and dynamic types need class and dataflow information.

rules.title: Write constructor member initializers in the canonical order
rules.summary: Constructor member initializer lists should be written in the actual initialization order, so no initializer reads a not-yet-initialized member.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Initializer list order differs from declaration order and one initializer uses a later-declared member.
rules.compliant_concept: Orders initializers to match base and member declaration order, avoiding dependencies on later members.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Out-of-order lists without cross-member dependencies are style issues, not defects.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires the class's member declaration order, which may live in another file.

rules.title: Gracefully handle self-copy assignment
rules.summary: User-provided copy assignment operators must leave both operands valid and unchanged when an object is assigned to itself.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Copy assignment deletes owned resources before copying from the source, breaking self-assignment.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses copy-and-swap, or checks for this == &rhs, or copies before releasing.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Operators safe by construction (copy-then-swap without explicit check) may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Unsafe release-then-copy ordering through helper functions requires dataflow.

rules.title: Do not use pointer-to-member operators to access nonexistent members
rules.summary: Pointer-to-member operators must only be applied to objects whose dynamic type actually contains the referenced member.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Converts a derived-member pointer to a base-member pointer and applies it to a pure base object.
rules.compliant_concept: Applies member pointers only to objects of the class containing the member; avoids null member pointers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Any .* or ->* on downcast member pointers looks similar even when the object type is correct.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires dynamic type tracking of objects and member-pointer provenance.

rules.title: Honor replacement handler requirements
rules.summary: Custom new, terminate, and unexpected handlers installed by the program must satisfy their required behaviors.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A new_handler returns without freeing memory, or a terminate handler returns to its caller.
rules.compliant_concept: Handlers free memory or throw bad_alloc, and terminate handlers end execution without returning.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Handlers that return under conditions where returning is permitted may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Handler identification and behavior analysis span registration and handler bodies across functions.

rules.title: Prefer special member functions and overloaded operators to C Standard Library functions
rules.summary: Prefer copy/compare/initialize via special member functions and operators instead of C byte functions like memcpy, memset, or memcmp on class objects.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses memset/memcpy/memcmp on non-trivially-copyable or non-standard-layout class objects.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses constructors, assignment, and comparison operators for class objects.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Byte functions on trivially copyable PODs are acceptable yet match name-based patterns.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Object triviality and layout depend on resolved types.

rules.title: Copy operations must not mutate the source object
rules.summary: Copy constructors and copy assignment operators must not modify the observable state of the source object.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A copy operation takes a non-const reference and alters the source, e.g., resetting its pointer.
rules.compliant_concept: Copy operations accept const references and leave the source unchanged; transfers use move operations.

exceptions.summary: Copy operations of reference-counted types like shared_ptr may update the source's reference count.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Mutation of non-salient bookkeeping such as reference counts would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Mutation via helper calls or mutable members needs semantic analysis.

rules.title: Guarantee that storage for strings has sufficient space for character data and the null terminator
rules.summary: Buffers receiving character data must be large enough for all characters plus the terminating null.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Extracts input into a fixed char array via operator>> without a width limit.
rules.compliant_concept: Reads into std::string, or sets stream width or checks lengths before copying.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Extraction into char arrays preceded by width() settings elsewhere may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Buffer sizes and data lengths flowing through variables need dataflow.

rules.title: Do not attempt to create a std::string from a null pointer
rules.summary: std::basic_string objects must not be constructed or assigned from a null character pointer.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Initializes std::string from getenv or another possibly-null pointer without checking.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks for null before constructing, or substitutes an empty string.
false_positive_risks: None expected; getenv can return null for any name.
false_negative_risks: Null pointers reaching std::string construction through variables or functions other than getenv are not tracked.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: std::string constructed directly from a null literal or an unchecked getenv() result.

rules.title: Use valid references, pointers, and iterators to reference elements of a basic_string
rules.summary: References, pointers, and iterators into a basic_string must not be used after string operations that may invalidate them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Keeps an iterator or c_str()/data() pointer across a modifying string call, then uses it.
rules.compliant_concept: Re-obtains iterators or pointers after modifying the string, using returned iterators where available.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Non-invalidating operations in between may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Invalidation in called functions or via aliased strings is missed.

rules.title: Range check element access
rules.summary: Position arguments to string element accessors and member functions must be within range; unchecked accessors need prior validation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Uses operator[], front(), or back() with unchecked indices or on a possibly empty string.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses at() with exception handling, or validates positions against size() first.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Indexes bounded by loop conditions or prior checks are still flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Index values and string sizes from callers or input need range analysis.
